title: Square-free words from lists of size three
credit: Posed by J. Grytczuk, J. Przybyło and X. Zhu (2011) in the context of nonrepetitive list colouring; see M. Rosenfeld (2022), V. Bui and M. Rosenfeld (2025).
premise_risks: Occasionally referred to as a conjecture of Grytczuk–Przybyło–Zhu; the usual name is 'the Thue choice number of the path is 3' (object named after Thue), so naming rule is likely satisfied but should be checked
plain: Thue showed in 1906 that there is an infinite word over three letters with no square, that is, no block immediately repeated (like 'abab'). Now suppose each position i has its own list A_i of three allowed symbols, chosen by an adversary from an unbounded alphabet. Is there always an infinite square-free word whose i-th letter lies in A_i? Lists of size 4 are known to suffice, and size 3 suffices when all lists are drawn from only four symbols.
math: Claim: for every sequence $(A_i)_{i\ge1}$ of sets $A_i\subseteq\mathbb N$ with $|A_i|=3$, there exists $w:\mathbb N_{\ge1}\to\mathbb N$ with $w(i)\in A_i$ for all $i$, such that there are no $i,k\ge1$ with $w(i+j)=w(i+k+j)$ for all $0\le j<k$. (By compactness, this is equivalent to the same statement for every finite length; that is, the Thue choice number of the path is $3$.)
